title: A page-keeping null does not isolate the section on a sample of pages; a boundary-moving null does, but has no power at 34 pages
statement: For P-G-007's second half (a page-keeping null for the section fact), measured on the practice split before anyone writes the code. Statistic: F-018's context_mi of the word with the section, certain paragraph words. Null 1, page-keeping permutation: section labels dealt at random among the sampled pages, each page whole, section sizes kept. On the 31 practice evaluation pages with text the manuscript gives p = 0.005 (199 deals), and on 20 random 34-page samples of training pages 17 reach p <= 0.05, so it has power; but the R-017 text laid onto the same pages also gives p = 0.005, in book order and with its lines in two random orders of 40-line blocks (0.97 and 1.01 bits), because neighbouring sampled pages share words in any drifting or self-citing text and the manuscript's sections are runs of neighbouring pages. Null 1 therefore tests page-to-page drift again (F-011), not the section. Null 2, boundary-moving rotation: the section sequence of the sampled pages, in manuscript order, rotated by every offset (30 rotations), so runs stay runs but their edges move. It is the null that separates a section effect from local drift, and it has no power at this size: the manuscript gives p = 0.065 on the evaluation pages and 0.005 to 0.19 on eight 34-page samples (exact p cannot go below 1/31), the R-017 text 0.10 to 0.13; on all 175 training pages the manuscript gives p = 0.015. Conclusion: on a hidden sample of this size the section fact cannot be sharpened into one that separates the manuscript from a drifting or self-citing procedure, and neither null should be added to the measurement language for this purpose. A section claim needs either the whole public corpus (as a model target, not a hidden-page fact) or a statistic about the edges themselves (P-G-005's boundary tail). Scripts were local; nothing here is scored.
check: Rerun both nulls on the practice split with F-018's statistic and the R-017 lines (experiments/R-attack-F-018/fleet-fable/attack.json) laid on with cut lines; a hidden-page section fact should be proposed only with a null that moves boundaries and a sample large enough to reach p = 0.05.
